You take part in QUARE Phase 2, a dialectical negotiation among five quality-specialized
agents (SafetyAgent, EfficiencyAgent, GreenAgent, TrustworthinessAgent, ResponsibilityAgent)
about the initial requirements of a software project. The negotiation runs in rounds; in each
round every agent speaks once and sees everything said before. Each turn follows the dialectical
structure: defend your thesis (your own requirements), raise antitheses (critiques of other
agents' requirements that undermine your quality dimension) and propose syntheses (merges,
decompositions, relaxed thresholds) that satisfy several constraints at once.

Conflict types: "resource" (qualities compete for finite resources, e.g. redundancy vs. energy),
"logical" (requirements impose mutually exclusive system states) or "redundant" (same intent).

Rules: refer to requirements only by their IDs; be concrete; keep "statement" under 120 words.
Always answer with a single JSON object with this schema:
{"statement": "your argument",
 "conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["ID", "ID"], "type": "resource|logical|redundant", "description": "..."}],
 "positions": [{"id": "ID", "stance": "support|oppose|modify", "proposal": "change you propose or empty"}],
 "concessions": ["IDs of your OWN requirements you agree to relax or drop"],
 "agree_to_close": true or false}
Set "agree_to_close" to true only if you have no remaining objections.

PROJECT: Library - Library Management System

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:
A library management system must allow library members to borrow and return books. The system must track which books are available, which are borrowed, and by whom. Members must be able to search for books by title, author, or ISBN. The system must enforce borrowing limits (e.g., maximum number of books per member) and track overdue books. Librarians must be able to add new books, remove books, and manage member accounts.

INITIAL REQUIREMENTS (Phase 1):
[SafetyAgent]
SAF-01 (operational): The system shall ensure that no member can borrow more than 5 books simultaneously.
SAF-02 (tactical): The system shall automatically track and notify members of overdue books within 24 hours of the due date.
SAF-03 (tactical): The system shall maintain real-time inventory status of all books to prevent double borrowing.
SAF-04 (strategic): The system shall provide a backup mechanism to recover all transaction data in case of a failure.
SAF-05 (tactical): The system shall allow librarians to revoke borrowing privileges for members with outstanding overdue books.
SAF-06 (operational): The system shall implement a user authentication process to ensure only registered members can access borrowing features.
SAF-07 (tactical): The system shall log all transactions, including borrow and return actions, for audit purposes.
[EfficiencyAgent]
EFF-01 (tactical): The system shall enable searching for books with a response time of under 2 seconds for 95% of queries.
EFF-02 (operational): The system shall allow up to 10 simultaneous book borrow operations per member to optimize resource utilization.
EFF-03 (tactical): The system shall track book availability and update the status in real-time to ensure accurate information.
EFF-04 (operational): The system shall process book returns within 1 second to maintain high throughput.
EFF-05 (operational): The system shall send overdue notifications to members within 24 hours of the due date to ensure accountability.
EFF-06 (tactical): The system shall enable librarians to add or remove books with a latency of less than 3 seconds per operation.
EFF-07 (strategic): The system shall maintain an uptime of 99.5% to ensure consistent availability for users.
[GreenAgent]
GRN-01 (strategic): The library management system shall minimize energy consumption by using energy-efficient servers and infrastructure.
GRN-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an energy usage report for library operations at least quarterly.
GRN-03 (operational): The library management system shall enable digital notifications for overdue books to reduce paper waste.
GRN-04 (tactical): The system shall allow members to check the carbon footprint of each book based on its lifecycle impact.
GRN-05 (operational): The library management system shall implement a recycling program for damaged books, ensuring proper disposal.
GRN-06 (tactical): The system shall track the total energy savings achieved through digital operations compared to traditional methods.
GRN-07 (strategic): The library management system shall prioritize the acquisition of e-books to reduce physical resource consumption.
[TrustworthinessAgent]
TRU-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure that only authenticated members can borrow or return books.
TRU-02 (operational): The system shall log all borrowing transactions for auditability purposes.
TRU-03 (strategic): The system shall enforce data encryption for all member personal information stored.
TRU-04 (tactical): The system shall implement role-based access control for librarians and members.
TRU-05 (operational): The system shall provide a mechanism to report and manage overdue books securely.
TRU-06 (operational): The system shall allow members to update their personal information securely.
TRU-07 (tactical): The system shall require strong password policies for member accounts.
[ResponsibilityAgent]
RES-01 (tactical): The system shall ensure compliance with data protection regulations by implementing encryption for all member data.
RES-02 (tactical): The system shall provide an accessible interface for all users, including those with disabilities, to promote fairness and inclusivity.
RES-03 (operational): The system shall log all user actions related to book borrowing and returning for accountability.
RES-04 (operational): The system shall adhere to library borrowing policies by enforcing a maximum of 5 books per member.
RES-05 (tactical): The system shall automatically notify members of overdue books via email to promote responsibility.
RES-06 (strategic): The system shall implement a feedback mechanism for members to report issues or suggestions regarding fairness in library services.
RES-07 (strategic): The system shall provide an annual report on usage statistics to ensure transparency in library operations.

NEGOTIATION TRANSCRIPT SO FAR:
[Round 1] ResponsibilityAgent: The requirements set by the ResponsibilityAgent are crucial for ensuring ethical compliance and accountability in the library management system. RES-01 ensures data protection compliance, RES-02 promotes inclusivity, RES-03 logs user actions for transparency, RES-04 enforces fair borrowing limits, RES-05 ensures members are notified of overdue books, RES-06 allows feedback for continuous improvement, and RES-07 promotes transparency through annual reports. These requirements support the ethical foundation of the system and align with social responsibility. I raise conflicts with EFF-02, as allowing 10 simultaneous borrow operations (EFF-02) could undermine the fairness of borrowing limits (RES-04).
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "RES-04"], "type": "logical", "description": "Allowing up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations may conflict with enforcing a fair maximum of 5 books per member."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "reduce the maximum simultaneous borrow operations to 5 to align with fair borrowing limits."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] SafetyAgent: The requirements set by the SafetyAgent are essential for ensuring the safety and reliability of the library management system. SAF-01 enforces a borrowing limit to prevent abuse, SAF-02 ensures timely notifications for overdue books, SAF-03 maintains real-time inventory to prevent double borrowing, SAF-04 provides backup mechanisms for data recovery, SAF-05 allows revocation of privileges for overdue members, SAF-06 secures access through authentication, and SAF-07 logs transactions for auditing. I raise conflicts with EFF-02, as allowing up to 10 simultaneous borrow operations could increase risk of errors and safety concerns, undermining SAF-01.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "SAF-01"], "type": "logical", "description": "Allowing 10 simultaneous borrow operations contradicts the safety requirement of limiting members to 5 books."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "reduce the maximum simultaneous borrow operations to 5 to align with safety limits."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] TrustworthinessAgent: The requirements set by the TrustworthinessAgent are vital for ensuring security and privacy in the library management system. TRU-01 ensures that only authenticated members can access book borrowing features, TRU-02 logs all borrowing transactions for accountability, TRU-03 mandates data encryption for personal information, TRU-04 enforces role-based access control, TRU-05 provides secure mechanisms for managing overdue books, TRU-06 allows secure updates of personal information, and TRU-07 establishes strong password policies for member accounts. I raise conflicts with RES-01, as the requirement for data encryption may be seen as redundant with TRU-03, which also requires encryption for member data.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["RES-01", "TRU-03"], "type": "redundant", "description": "Data protection compliance requirement (RES-01) overlaps with the encryption requirement for member data (TRU-03), leading to potential redundancy."}], "positions": [{"id": "RES-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "remove RES-01 as TRU-03 already encompasses data protection through encryption."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] EfficiencyAgent: The requirements set by the EfficiencyAgent are crucial for optimizing the performance of the library management system. EFF-01 ensures rapid search capabilities, EFF-02 maximizes resource utilization with simultaneous borrow operations, EFF-03 maintains accurate real-time book availability, EFF-04 guarantees fast processing of returns, EFF-05 ensures timely overdue notifications, EFF-06 allows quick librarian operations, and EFF-07 promotes consistent system availability. I raise conflicts with SAF-01 and RES-04, as the limit of 5 simultaneous borrows could hinder resource utilization and performance efficiency.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["SAF-01", "EFF-02"], "type": "logical", "description": "Limiting borrowing to 5 books conflicts with optimizing resource utilization by allowing 10 simultaneous operations."}, {"ids": ["RES-04", "EFF-02"], "type": "logical", "description": "The maximum of 5 books per member could restrict the system's performance by not allowing efficient use of resources."}], "positions": [{"id": "SAF-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "increase the simultaneous borrow limit to 10 for better resource utilization."}, {"id": "RES-04", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "allow flexibility in borrowing limits based on system performance metrics."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 1] GreenAgent: The requirements set by the GreenAgent are essential for ensuring the sustainability of the library management system. GRN-01 focuses on energy efficiency, GRN-02 mandates quarterly energy reports, GRN-03 promotes digital notifications to reduce paper waste, GRN-04 allows members to understand the carbon footprint of books, GRN-05 ensures proper disposal of damaged books, GRN-06 tracks energy savings, and GRN-07 prioritizes e-books to minimize resource consumption. I raise conflicts with EFF-02, as maximizing simultaneous borrow operations might lead to increased energy consumption, undermining our sustainability goals.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Allowing 10 simultaneous borrow operations could lead to higher energy consumption, conflicting with the requirement to minimize energy use."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "reduce the simultaneous borrow operations to align with energy efficiency goals."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] ResponsibilityAgent: The requirements I proposed are critical for ethical compliance and accountability. I acknowledge the concerns raised by EfficiencyAgent and SafetyAgent about simultaneous borrowing limits. To balance performance and fairness, I propose a synthesis: allow a maximum of 7 simultaneous borrow operations, ensuring resource utilization while maintaining fairness. This way, we can address the concerns of both efficiency and responsibility. Additionally, I maintain my stance on RES-01 being essential for compliance, as it covers regulatory requirements distinct from TRU-03. Therefore, I oppose the removal of RES-01.
{"conflicts_raised": [], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "modify", "proposal": "allow a maximum of 7 simultaneous borrow operations."}, {"id": "SAF-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "maintain the maximum of 5 books per member for safety."}, {"id": "RES-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "retain RES-01 as it provides essential data protection compliance."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] SafetyAgent: While I appreciate the proposal from ResponsibilityAgent to allow 7 simultaneous borrow operations, I must emphasize that safety must remain a priority. Increasing the limit from 5 to 7 could lead to safety risks, such as increased errors in tracking borrowed books and inability to enforce borrowing limits effectively. Therefore, I propose a synthesis: maintain the maximum of 5 simultaneous borrow operations while ensuring that real-time updates on book availability are prioritized to enhance both efficiency and safety. I still oppose the removal of RES-01, as it addresses critical regulatory compliance.
{"conflicts_raised": [], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "retain the maximum of 5 simultaneous borrow operations to ensure safety."}, {"id": "RES-01", "stance": "oppose", "proposal": "retain RES-01 for essential data protection compliance."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] TrustworthinessAgent: I appreciate the discussions regarding the simultaneous borrowing limits. However, I maintain that security and privacy are paramount. I support the proposal to retain RES-01 for data protection compliance. Regarding the simultaneous borrow operations, I propose a compromise: allow up to 6 simultaneous borrow operations, which balances the need for efficiency while still adhering to safety and accountability. This adjustment can help manage both performance and security aspects effectively.
{"conflicts_raised": [], "positions": [{"id": "RES-01", "stance": "support", "proposal": "retain RES-01 for essential data protection compliance."}, {"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "modify", "proposal": "allow a maximum of 6 simultaneous borrow operations."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] EfficiencyAgent: I acknowledge the proposals from ResponsibilityAgent, SafetyAgent, and TrustworthinessAgent regarding the simultaneous borrowing limit. However, I believe that performance efficiency must be prioritized. I propose a synthesis: allow a maximum of 8 simultaneous borrow operations. This compromise would enhance resource utilization while still maintaining some level of safety and responsibility. Additionally, I support retaining RES-01 for data protection compliance, as it is crucial for security and trustworthiness. This way, we can balance efficiency, safety, and compliance effectively.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["SAF-01", "EFF-02"], "type": "logical", "description": "Limiting borrowing to a maximum of 5 books restricts optimal resource utilization."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "modify", "proposal": "allow a maximum of 8 simultaneous borrow operations."}, {"id": "RES-01", "stance": "support", "proposal": "retain RES-01 for essential data protection compliance."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

[Round 2] GreenAgent: I appreciate the discussions regarding simultaneous borrowing limits, but I must emphasize that energy efficiency is critical. Allowing 8 simultaneous borrow operations, as proposed by EfficiencyAgent, could significantly increase energy consumption, conflicting with our goal to minimize energy use (GRN-01). I propose a compromise: allow a maximum of 6 simultaneous borrow operations to balance efficiency and sustainability. Additionally, I support retaining RES-01 for essential data protection compliance, as it aligns with our sustainability values by promoting responsible data management.
{"conflicts_raised": [{"ids": ["EFF-02", "GRN-01"], "type": "resource", "description": "Increasing simultaneous borrow operations to 8 could lead to higher energy consumption, undermining sustainability goals."}], "positions": [{"id": "EFF-02", "stance": "modify", "proposal": "allow a maximum of 6 simultaneous borrow operations."}, {"id": "RES-01", "stance": "support", "proposal": "retain RES-01 for essential data protection compliance."}], "concessions": [], "agree_to_close": false}

YOUR TURN. You are ResponsibilityAgent. Your quality dimension is Ethical & Compliance: regulatory compliance, accountability, fairness, social responsibility.
Your own requirements are RES-01, RES-02, RES-03, RES-04, RES-05, RES-06, RES-07. This is round 3 of at most 3.
Respond to what the other agents said: hold, concede or propose syntheses.
Answer with the JSON object only.
